scope: Current and former federal elected officials and executive-branch appointees since 2017, from any party.

entries.name: Robert Menendez
entries.matter: Bribery, acting as an agent of Egypt, obstruction
entries.summary: Convicted by a federal jury in July 2024. Sentenced in January 2025 to 11 years in prison and reported to prison in June 2025.

entries.name: George Santos
entries.summary: Expelled from the House in December 2023. Pleaded guilty in August 2024 and was sentenced in April 2025 to 87 months. President Trump commuted the sentence in October 2025.

entries.name: Henry Cuellar
entries.summary: Indicted in May 2024 on charges of taking bribes linked to Azerbaijan and a Mexican bank. Pleaded not guilty. President Trump pardoned him in December 2025, before trial.

entries.name: Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick
entries.matter: Theft of about $5 million in FEMA funds, illegal campaign contributions
entries.summary: Indicted in November 2025. A House Ethics investigative subcommittee reported in March 2026 that it found she violated House rules and federal law. The criminal case is listed as pending until a verdict is verified.
entries.statusDetail: House Ethics finding, criminal case pending

entries.name: Duncan Hunter
entries.summary: Pleaded guilty in December 2019 and was sentenced in 2020 to 11 months in prison. President Trump pardoned him in December 2020.

entries.name: Chris Collins
entries.matter: Securities fraud conspiracy (insider trading tip), false statements to the FBI
entries.summary: Pleaded guilty in October 2019 and was sentenced in January 2020 to 26 months in prison. President Trump pardoned him in December 2020.

entries.name: Ryan Zinke
entries.matter: Misuse of official position, misleading investigators
entries.summary: The Interior Department Inspector General reported in February 2022 that he misused his position over a Montana development project, and in August 2022 that he knowingly misled investigators. No criminal charges were filed.

entries.name: Steve Bannon
entries.matter: Fraud in the We Build the Wall fundraiser
entries.summary: Federal fraud charges filed in 2020 ended with a presidential pardon in January 2021. In February 2025 he pleaded guilty in New York state court to scheming to defraud donors and received a conditional discharge with no jail time.
entries.statusDetail: State guilty plea; federal case pardoned

entries.name: Tom Homan
entries.office: White House Border Czar (2025 to present)
entries.matter: Reported acceptance of $50,000 in cash from undercover FBI agents in 2024
entries.summary: News reports in September 2025 said an FBI sting recorded him accepting cash before he took office, and that the investigation was closed in 2025. The White House said he did nothing wrong. No charges have been filed.
